title: Associativity of finite pro-etale derived pullback comparisons
statement:
Let $j:W\to Z$, $h:Z\to Y$, and $k:Y\to X$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Fix a finite commutative ring $A$, with constant coefficient sheaves $A_T$ on their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and canonical coefficient identifications [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Let $Lf^*$ be the ordinary unbounded derived module pullback [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $c_{f,g}:L(g\circ f)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*\circ Lg^*$ for the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], with the canonical constant coefficient identifications; its source is the pullback $L(g\circ f)^*$ formed with the canonical identification of the composite, which agrees with the composite identification required by that lemma by [lem-trf-constant-coefficient-composition]. For every $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_X)$ the equality
$$Lj^*(c_{h,k}(M))\circ c_{j,k\circ h}(M)=c_{j,h}(Lk^*M)\circ c_{h\circ j,k}(M):L(k\circ h\circ j)^*M\longrightarrow Lj^*Lh^*Lk^*M$$
holds after the canonical functor associator. The comparisons are the ones normalized by the termwise module pullback maps on K-flat complexes with flat terms in the cited composition lemma; no arbitrary choice of composition isomorphisms is allowed.

proof.text: Compute both ordinary direct-image composition paths on a module N and a test object U. Apply the specified section formula for d, the sectionwise pushforward map and restriction formulas, and equality induction for transport along scheme associativity. The generic fibre-product identity MorphismProperty.Over.pullbackComp_assoc, with its equality transport made explicit, identifies the two pasting maps. The contravariant presheaf composition law then identifies the section maps. Extensionality gives coherence of the direct-image natural isomorphisms.

proof.text: Compare any two normalized ordinary module adjunctions by equality of their units on every section. Hence a is the inverse of leftAdjointCompIso for fixed normalized adjunctions and d. Apply leftAdjointCompIso_assoc to the six adjunctions and the direct-image coherence equation. Equality induction handles the triple-composite transport. Invert the natural-isomorphism equality and evaluate it on modules to obtain the ordinary pullback cocycle. The same conjugate-unit identity gives the ordinary comparison on successive unit sections. Equality of normalized adjunction units identifies the actual supplied adjunctions; the direct-image section formula then gives restriction along fibre-product pasting. Expose this unit formula together with the ordinary comparison and its exact-derived identification as proEtaleConstantRingPullbackComposition_ordinary, without exposing the chosen witnesses.

The module pullbacks in this interface are exact, and their derived pullbacks are mapDerivedCategory. For a:H≅F⋙G, the composite mapDerivedCategoryNatIso a followed by mapDerivedCategoryCompIso F G satisfies the representative factorization on every complex: use mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_hom_app_factors and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac. The termwise b equals mapHomologicalComplex a by extensionality on degrees. Retain the K-flat preservation and flatness conjuncts of the existing characterization. Its uniqueness therefore identifies each specified canonical derived comparison with this exact-derived composite. This verifies the original normalization without selecting a new resolution.

proof.text: Apply mapDerivedCategoryNatIso to the ordinary cocycle. Its compatibility with composition, left and right whiskering, together with mapDerivedCategoryCompIso_assoc, proves the derived cocycle as an equality of natural transformations. Equality induction identifies mapDerivedCategoryNatIso of the ordinary associativity transport with the transport of the derived pullback. Evaluate on M and replace each exact-derived comparison by the specified canonical comparison using the preceding uniqueness argument.

For the underlying abelian inverse-image comparison used to normalize the stalk calculation, specialize ringUnitComparison of the ring-sheaf change adjunction to the specified constant coefficient identification and its module adjunction. This proves proEtaleConstantRingPullback_underlyingUnit_isIso. Its public statement lets the stalk proof use the unit comparison without importing all private implementation details of the ring-sheaf adjunction module.

New node lem-trf-adjoint-composition-coherence is an exact Mathlib leaf; I checked it against CompositionIso.lean:64-80,157-184 and Mates.lean:311. With e_ijk=d_ijk^{-1}, Mathlib's hypothesis h, read in components, is the inverse of the node's d-cocycle. unit_conjugateEquiv_symm, with adj1=adj_ik, adj2=the composite and alpha=d, gives the node's unit equation. The component of the conclusion at M is the displayed a-equation. It tests correctly on identity adjunctions, one-object categories and empty categories. It is not a duplicate of lem-sc-left-adjoint-composition-iso-associativity, which is the special case where the functors are equal: (kh)_*N(U)=N(Z x_X U) and k_*h_*N(U)=N(Z x_Y(Y x_X U)) are only isomorphic. lem-pc-derived-pullback-assoc-kflat concerns Zariski O_X-modules, a different coefficient category. Item: Step 1 applies the constant-coefficient composition to all four pairs, which is what the composition lemma requires. Step 2: the variance of d=N(e_U^{-1}) is right and the cocycle follows from fibre-product uniqueness, so the elementary marking is fair. Step 3's unit-compatible conjugate is the same normalization the composition lemma uses for its termwise canonical isomorphism. Its tensor formula silently uses that inverse image commutes with tensor products, but nothing later depends on that formula. Step 4's index and inversion orders match the item. Steps 5-6 follow Stacks 0D6D's representative proof with 06YS and 0G7E, and the naturality cancellation is written out. Pullbacks are K-flat for arbitrary ringed-topos morphisms; no boundedness or scheme flatness is assumed, and W empty is covered.
